health.summary: Your bloodwork is strong overall — 90%+ of markers in optimal range. Big wins: testosterone jumped 17% and Vitamin D nearly doubled. Five things need attention, and three of them are already trending the right direction.

wins.title: Testosterone surging
wins.detail: Up 17% from 481 to 564 ng/dL. Free T up 23% too. Whatever you're doing — keep doing it.

wins.title: Vitamin D dialed in
wins.detail: Jumped from 30 to 52. You were borderline insufficient, now you're solidly optimal.

wins.title: DHEA-S up 62%
wins.detail: 180 to 291. This is your body's hormone building block — strong recovery.

wins.title: Heart inflammation low
wins.detail: hs-CRP at 0.7 — puts you in the lowest cardiovascular risk category.

wins.title: Blood sugar excellent
wins.detail: Fasting glucose 85, A1c 5.1% — no insulin resistance anywhere in sight.

recommendations.title: Start magnesium supplementation
recommendations.why: Your RBC magnesium dropped from 4.4 to 3.7 — now below the healthy range. Magnesium affects sleep, muscle recovery, stress response, and heart rhythm.
recommendations.action: Take 400mg magnesium glycinate or threonate before bed. Glycinate is better for sleep, threonate crosses the blood-brain barrier. Retest in 3 months.

recommendations.title: Increase omega-3 dose
recommendations.why: You went from 3.8% to 4.7% — great progress, but still below the 5.5% optimal target. Low omega-3 is tied to higher cardiac risk and inflammation.
recommendations.action: Bump fish oil to 3g combined EPA+DHA daily (most capsules are 1g, so 3 caps/day). Or eat fatty fish 3-4x per week. This should push you over 5.5% by next draw.

recommendations.title: Address small dense LDL
recommendations.why: Your overall LDL particle count improved, but the small dense particles (the dangerous kind) went from 221 to 299. These are more likely to lodge in artery walls.
recommendations.action: Cut refined carbs and added sugar — these are the #1 driver of small dense LDL (not dietary fat). Consider adding citrus bergamot or berberine. Increase soluble fiber (oats, beans, psyllium). Discuss with your provider at next visit.

recommendations.title: Keep estradiol trending down
recommendations.why: At 46 (ref <=39), it's mildly elevated for a male. It dropped from 53, so the trend is right. High estradiol in men can mean excess aromatase activity — your body converting testosterone to estrogen.
recommendations.action: Eat more cruciferous vegetables (broccoli, cauliflower, Brussels sprouts) — they contain DIM which helps metabolize estrogen. Limit alcohol. Maintain healthy body fat %. No action needed if it keeps dropping.

recommendations.title: Maintain your current protocol
recommendations.why: Testosterone, Vitamin D, and DHEA-S all made huge jumps. Your cardiovascular markers, metabolic panel, liver, kidneys, thyroid, and PSA are all textbook optimal.
recommendations.action: Don't change what's working. Keep your current Vitamin D and any testosterone-support supplements. Next Function Health draw around October — we'll track whether these trends hold.
